rows.name: Capacitive soil moisture probe v1.2 (analog out)

dims_mm.notes: 98 x 23 x 4 mm, 15 g (Probots page). The probe sits outside the shell: probe end in the soil, electronics end above it; only its lead enters the shell, through a cable exit.

mount.notes: Not mounted in the shell: pushed into the pot's soil up to its line. Its lead passes a strain-relieved cable exit in the shell wall.

pins.name: AO
pins.notes: analog out, lower when the soil is wetter (relative reading, per-unit calibration); listed as AOUT by vendors

pins.name: VCC
pins.notes: 3.3-5.5 V (Probots page); powered from the J_IO 3.3 V pin

module_connector.notes: Probots lists 'PH2.54-3P', 'Supports 3-Pin Gravity Sensor interface' (Gravity order signal, +, -). The physical order and whether a Dupont 1x3 harness end mates this socket are UNVERIFIED (first article).

aperture.notes: 6.5 mm lead exit through the shell wall with an inner strain-relief clamp (two posts and a cable-tie slot); the probe stays outside, water stays outside the shell.

electrical.logic_v: analog 0-3.3 V at a 3.3 V supply (range UNVERIFIED)

firmware.driver_notes: analogRead on the J_IO SIG (ADC1: GPIO4/5/6, usable with Wi-Fi on), 16-sample average, mapped to 0-100 % between the dry and wet calibration readings (sensor_display settings soil_raw_dry, soil_raw_wet), clamped.

kicad.notes: Plugs into J_IO1..3; no backplane change.

uncertain: clone boards with an NE555 (needs 4.5 V) or with no regulator can misbehave at 3.3 V: incoming check at 3.3 V before fitting
some boards miss the R4-to-GND link (hackmd note), so the reading never settles
the reading is relative, not volumetric water content: per-unit dry/wet calibration
the electronics end is not waterproof: it must stay above the soil (conformal coat recommended)
connector pin order and the Dupont 1x3 fit on the board's socket (first article)
Robocraze price is a search snippet, not a page read
never built or measured by us: all checks are digital

manual.selftest: the soil reading changes when the probe goes into damp soil
manual.care: Push the probe into the soil only up to its line; keep the electronics end above the soil and dry.

port.why: J_IO SIG = GPIO4/5/6 = ESP32-S3 ADC1, readable with Wi-Fi on; 3.3 V supply only (clone probes that need 5 V fail the incoming check).

rows.name: Vertical float level switch (PP, dry reed contact)

reference_product.mpn_or_model: Water level float sensor switch, vertical

dims_mm.notes: Not on the page read. UNVERIFIED typical: M10 stem, about 52-58 mm long, about 24 mm float. It sits outside the shell, in the tank; only its lead enters the shell, through a cable exit.

mount.notes: Not mounted in the shell: fitted in the tank (a clip-on holder over the rim is preferred to a hole in the tank). Its lead passes a strain-relieved cable exit in the shell wall.

pins.name: SIG
pins.notes: reed contact lead 1; read with the ESP32 internal pull-up

module_connector.location: two bare leads from the stem
module_connector.notes: 8 cm cable (Probots). Dry contact: either lead can be SIG.

backplane_harness.backplane_connector: JST_PH_2.0_3P (J_IO1..3); factory pre-wired lead, 3V3 position empty

aperture.notes: 6.5 mm lead exit through the shell wall with an inner strain-relief clamp; the float stays in the tank, water stays outside the shell.

electrical.supply_v: n/a (dry contact; rated 100 V DC, 0.5 A, 50 W per Probots)

firmware.driver_notes: INPUT_PULLUP on the J_IO SIG, debounced (water sloshes). Contact closed = water up (OK); open = tank low. An unplugged or broken lead reads as low, so a fault warns instead of staying quiet.

kicad.notes: Plugs into J_IO1..3 (pins 1 GND and 3 SIG); no backplane change.

uncertain: normally open or closed depends on which way the float is fitted on its stem: fit it so the contact closes when the water is up; the self-test shows the live state
whether the listing's 'digital output' means anything beyond a reed contact
the Robocraze price is a search snippet, not a page read (ElectronicsComp Rs 99 ex GST snippet left out: vendor not in the merge list)
never built or measured by us: all checks are digital

manual.selftest: the water reading says OK with the float lifted and LOW with it hanging down
manual.care: Fit the float so the contact closes when the water is up; keep the gadget itself away from the water.

port.why: Dry contact between port pins 1 (GND) and 3 (SIG), read with the internal pull-up; the 3V3 pin is not used.

prewire.note: The factory solders a JST-PH 3-pin lead (stock: CABLE_JSTPH_3P_<len> with the module-end housing cut off; length = the design's harness length class) to the float's two leads, sleeves the joints with heat-shrink and leaves the 3V3 wire cut back and insulated. It plugs into the J_IO port. The maker never solders.

prompt_rules: A soil probe and a float switch can watch a plant pot or a water tank: the gadget shows soil moisture and a tank-low warning on its screen or light and on its own page on the home Wi-Fi (no push messages). It cannot water the plant (no pump yet), and a light strip is not a grow light.

The probe and the float stay outside the shell in the pot or tank; their leads come in through a cable exit on the back or a side, at least 50 mm up from the bottom (the core board fills the bottom), and the gadget itself stays dry next to the pot or tank.

Use behaviour template sensor_display for soil and tank readings; the soil probe needs a per-probe dry and wet calibration (settings soil_raw_dry and soil_raw_wet), and the reading is relative moisture, not a lab measurement.
